participants: Bryan Ostermiller (external mindset/performance coach, not Primal Instinct)
summary: A roughly 51-minute one-to-one coaching session in which Harry Edmonds is the paying client and Bryan Ostermiller is his external mindset coach — no prospect is present and no Primal Instinct business is transacted, so this sits outside the sales corpus entirely. Proposed subtype label for later clustering: 'rep_external_coaching'. Harry describes hitting a wall the previous week chasing his monthly bonus, deciding to let it go, telling his manager he was taking the rest of the month off and blocking his calendar, and then unexpectedly being told he had hit bonus anyway. The session runs on Hawkins' consciousness framework — pride, courage, power versus force — with Bryan advising Harry to stop optimising his twenties for income, move to Thailand, cap sales at five hours a day and spend the rest on training, learning and investing. The last ten minutes cover Harry's own renewal with Bryan (price unchanged, Harry raises finances as his concern), book recommendations, and whether to get a neck tattoo.
notable: Compensation and bonus mechanics: Harry believed the monthly bonus was measured on new cash collected and not payment plans, and was told otherwise — 'Angelo messages me the next morning, by the way, you hit your bonus. I was like, what? Because I thought it was on new cash, not payment plans.' This sits directly against the pressure applied in the 28 May 1-1 to convert payment plans into paid-in-full.

Rep income disclosure: 'I did 7k this month, six and a half last month' in commissions; a colleague, Farooq, is reported at '21k this month in comms'. Cross-references the $600 per deal figure Harry quoted to Ken Baracaldo on 28 May.

Corpus gap by choice: Harry states he told Chris he was taking the rest of the month off and blocking his calendar with no fixed return date — 'I'm gonna take the rest of the month off and I'm gonna block my calendar out for next week and when I'm ready I'm just gonna open it back up.' At the end of this call he confirms he will reopen it 'when I'm ready'. Any thin patch in this rep's late-May/early-June call record is deliberate, not a recording failure.
A payment-plan client voluntarily increased their payment mid-term: 'I get texts from one of my leads. payment planned earlier in the month saying, Hey, can I put another 3k down?'

Harry recounts pitching a couple while visibly angry and privately contemptuous of their asking the price before deciding — 'they said something that really pissed me off... The husband whispered in her and she said, yeah, how much is it so we can think about it? I was like, no, just get me to think about it before you even know how much it costs.' They came back the following day and paid in full.

Harry has personal experience of a coaching payment plan causing him hardship — 'I did 3K a month on a payment plan. And then one month I did 3K and I was like, can't pay for rent' — which is notable against the open-wallet and instalment pressure he is being coached to apply to prospects.

Relocation and scheduling: Harry plans to move to Thailand and take sales calls 19:00 to midnight local time, noting 'Chris is like, you have to be on the team meeting no matter what' and that he can only take five calls a day on that time zone. Expect a change in his call volume and timestamps from that point.

Bryan explicitly distinguishes coaching from directive advice — 'as a coach, I don't really give you shoulds or tell people exactly what to do unless they're in danger' — before switching to a 'little brother' frame to give direct life advice. A cleaner consent practice than anything in the sales calls reviewed.

Bryan on his own business model, relevant as a contrast to the Primal Instinct offer: 'our community is entirely referral driven. The way I do coaching doesn't have like a trademark process behind it. And I don't make any big claims. These big guarantees.'

Diarization is unreliable in stretches — short turns are repeatedly merged across labels (e.g. at 00:08:47 and 00:10:06 the speakers invert mid-passage). Roles were read from content: Bryan is the American with a wife and newborn who wired the IRS $52,000; Harry is the 22-year-old British closer.
